newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH PIONEER BALANCED FUND UP 716 PCT SINCE 1992.
newsitem.headline: POLISH PIONEER BALANCED FUND UP 716 PCT SINCE 1992.

text.p: The Pioneer First Polish Trust Fund Company, owned by Boston-based Pioneer Group, has increased the value of its balanced fund unit by 716.1 percent since its start in July 1992, the group's President said.
"As an original investor I'm delighted to see net asset value up over 700 percent," John Cogan told a news conference on Monday on the fund's fifth anniversary.
Miroslaw Lubon, the Polish company's spokesman, said the firm's bond-based fund, selling units since June 1995, had raised net asset value by 37.4 percent.
He said the aggressive fund, selling units since December 1995, had lifted net asset value by 119.3 percent.
Alicja Malecka, the president of Pioneer in Poland, said the firm would expand its products as more instruments became traded in the country, such as derivatives, but would not give details.
The Warsaw bourse is considering introducing trade in derivatives around the third quarter this year.
